subject: Architecture
title: Floating Bridges for Rising Seas
description: A micro-lesson that makes Floating Bridges for Rising Seas usable.

hook.text: Norway is designing floating bridges across fjords that are too deep for any foundation — up to 4,000 feet deep.

buildup.text: Submerged pontoons hold the bridge deck at road level while the fjord floor stays impossibly far below.

discovery.text: The E39 Coastal Highway project plans to replace seven ferry crossings with fixed links — including floating spans.

twist.text: Climate change and rising seas may make floating infrastructure essential for coastal cities worldwide.

climax.text: Seattle already has the world's longest floating bridge — 7,710 feet across Lake Washington.

punchline.text: When the water is too deep for foundations, let the bridge float.

quiz.question: Why is Norway developing floating bridges?
options: To reduce environmental impact on marine ecosystems
Fjords are too deep for any conventional foundation
Floating bridges are cheaper than underwater tunnels
